text:
Matty Beniers looks like the player the Kraken drafted second overall again. Sixteen points in 23 games, five on the power play, and 18:13 a night as Seattle's top center, with a line alongside Kaapo Kakko and Samoskevich that Alison Lukan, who covers the team, keeps calling the one driving play.

The underlying numbers back it up. His own chances run at 0.85 expected goals per 60 minutes, right where he was last season, and the team is 6.5 points better in share of expected goals at five on five with him on the ice than without him. Seven goals on 5.9 expected is only mildly lucky. Where the luck shows is around him: his linemates and goalies have run hot, about four goals better than the chances suggest, which is why his points per 60 (2.30) sit at the top of our talent range rather than the middle.

That is worth remembering because Evolving-Hockey's 2025-26 numbers flagged the same pattern last year. Watch the shots: 18 in his last four games. If the volume holds, the points can survive a cooler run of puck luck.
